READ-ONLY line-by-line audit of /workspace/SuperGrok1.5 (H100 scope) — region A2: the C++ binding layer. Do NOT edit. CPU-side commands OK (grep, nm/cuobjdump on the .so), no GPU, no builds.

FILES (every line): csrc/bindings/bindings.cpp (~3500 lines, recently modified: SG2 slows threading + SG11 lamb_eff change + fused_step m.def), csrc/bindings/helpers.h, csrc/bindings/dispatch.cpp (PROVISIONAL — a sibling agent is actively refactoring it; tag findings there as provisional and do not deep-dive its in-flux fused_step section).

AUDIT DIMENSIONS, for EVERY binding function:
1. **Input validation completeness**: tensor dtype/device/contiguity/numel checks before data_ptr use; vector-length agreement (e.g. params/grads/mus/slows lists must be same length — verify EVERY multi-tensor binding checks ALL its lists, the recently-added slows included); int overflow at int32 boundaries (numel > 2^31); null/empty handling; TORCH_CHECK vs silent UB.
2. **Stream/synchronization correctness**: every kernel launch on the current torch stream (c10::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream) — flag any default-stream launch or missing stream arg; any cudaDeviceSynchronize that should be stream-scoped; events/sync before host reads of device results (e.g. prodigy's returned d/r/s scalars — how do they get to host? sync correctness?).
3. **Memory management**: every temporary allocation (torch::empty/zeros inside bindings) — lifetime vs async kernel use (a temp freed at scope end while the kernel still runs on-stream is use-after-free unless caching allocator stream-safety covers it — verify allocations use the same stream); persistent caches/statics (thread safety, growth bounds); the FusedScratch cache keyed by (device,n) — eviction policy (unbounded growth?).
4. **GIL handling**: long device-synchronous sections holding the GIL (py::gil_scoped_release usage or absence); callbacks into Python.
5. **Error paths**: CUDA error checks after launches (cudaGetLastError discipline) — flag every launch with no error check; exception safety (partial state mutation before a throw).
6. **ABI/signature drift**: m.def declarations vs the actual C++ signatures vs how Python calls them (cross-check grokking_optimizers/optimizers/*.py call sites arg-by-arg for ALL 11 optimizers — position and count; the recent slows insertion is exactly the kind of place an off-by-one hides).
7. **Dead bindings**: exported functions nothing calls (cross-ref Python callers); duplicated logic that should be shared.
OUTPUT: markdown — per-binding table (function × dimensions, OK/ISSUE + file:line), every ISSUE with severity (CRITICAL=UB/corruption, HIGH=wrong-under-conditions, MED=robustness, LOW=hygiene) and a precise fix spec. Line-by-line discipline: cite specific lines, not impressions.

106	// ── Boundary validation for optimizer fused-step entrypoints ─────────
107	// The Python wrappers historically owned device/dtype/shape/contiguity
108	// invariants; these binding entrypoints trusted them. A non-contiguous param
109	// view, a device/dtype mismatch between param and grad, or a shape mismatch
110	// silently corrupts the in-place fused update (the launchers index a flat
111	// pointer with the param's numel). Validate at the C++ boundary so a bad call
112	// fails loudly. `where` is the entrypoint name for the error message.
113	//
114	// We check the param against its paired grad. Optimizer-state buffers (m, v,
115	// ema, …) are allocated by the wrapper from `torch.zeros_like(param)` so they
116	// inherit the param's device/dtype/shape/contiguity; the param check is the
117	// load-bearing one. A missing/empty grad (sparse-grad fallback) is skipped —
118	// the per-op loops already filter those out before dispatch.
119	inline void check_param_grad(
120	    const torch::Tensor& p,
121	    const torch::Tensor& g,
122	    const char* where
123	) {
124	    TORCH_CHECK(p.defined(), where, ": param tensor is undefined");
125	#if defined(WITH_HIP)
126	    TORCH_CHECK(p.is_hip(), where, ": param must be on a HIP device");
127	#else
128	    TORCH_CHECK(p.is_cuda(), where, ": param must be on a CUDA device");
129	#endif
130	    // A non-contiguous param view aliases a strided storage; the fused
131	    // launchers treat data_ptr() as a dense [numel] buffer, so a strided view
132	    // would read/write the wrong elements and silently corrupt the update.
133	    TORCH_CHECK(p.is_contiguous(), where,
134	                ": param must be contiguous (got a non-contiguous view); "
135	                "call .contiguous() in the Python wrapper before the fused step");
136	    if (!g.defined() || g.numel() == 0) return;  // sparse-grad: skip (filtered)
137	    TORCH_CHECK(g.device() == p.device(), where,
138	                ": grad device (", g.device().str(),
139	                ") != param device (", p.device().str(), ")");
140	    TORCH_CHECK(g.scalar_type() == p.scalar_type(), where,
141	                ": grad dtype (", toString(g.scalar_type()),
142	                ") != param dtype (", toString(p.scalar_type()), ")");
143	    TORCH_CHECK(g.sizes() == p.sizes(), where,
144	                ": grad shape (", g.sizes(), ") != param shape (",
145	                p.sizes(), ")");
146	    TORCH_CHECK(g.is_contiguous(), where, ": grad must be contiguous");
147	}

149	// Validate every (param, grad) pair in a multi-tensor fused-step entrypoint.
150	inline void check_params_grads(
151	    const std::vector<torch::Tensor>& params,
152	    const std::vector<torch::Tensor>& grads,
153	    const char* where
154	) {
155	    TORCH_CHECK(params.size() == grads.size(), where,
156	                ": params.size() (", params.size(),
157	                ") != grads.size() (", grads.size(), ")");
158	    for (size_t i = 0; i < params.size(); ++i)
159	        check_param_grad(params[i], grads[i], where);

162	// ── Device-side gradient clipping: single CPU sync instead of N ──────
163	inline void clip_grad_norms_device_side(
164	    std::vector<torch::Tensor>& grads,
165	    size_t n_params,
166	    float grad_clip_norm
167	) {
168	    if (grad_clip_norm <= 0.0f) return;
169	
170	    // Collect the present grads once. Fused multi-tensor ops want a flat list.
171	    std::vector<torch::Tensor> present;
172	    present.reserve(n_params);
173	    for (size_t i = 0; i < n_params; i++) {
174	        if (grads[i].defined() && grads[i].numel() > 0)
175	            present.push_back(grads[i]);
176	    }
177	    if (present.empty()) return;
178	
179	    // Per-tensor L2 norms via a single fused multi-tensor reduction
180	    // (torch::_foreach_norm), replacing the per-tensor upcast + dot + add_
181	    // (≈2N kernel launches) with one foreach launch. Numerics: the L2 norm of
182	    // each tensor is accumulated into a fp32 sum-of-squares (squaring the
183	    // per-tensor norm == that tensor's sum-of-squares), matching the original
184	    // fp32 accumulation of the global sum-of-squares. To preserve the original
185	    // precision when grads are NOT already fp32, upcast those (only) to fp32
186	    // before the norm; fp32 grads skip the upcast entirely.
187	    bool all_fp32 = true;
188	    for (auto& g : present)
189	        if (g.scalar_type() != torch::kFloat32) { all_fp32 = false; break; }
190	
191	    std::vector<torch::Tensor> norm_inputs;
192	    if (all_fp32) {
193	        norm_inputs = present;
194	    } else {
195	        norm_inputs.reserve(present.size());
196	        for (auto& g : present)
197	            norm_inputs.push_back(g.scalar_type() == torch::kFloat32
198	                                      ? g
199	                                      : g.to(torch::kFloat32));
200	    }
201	
202	    auto norms = torch::_foreach_norm(norm_inputs, /*p=*/2);
203	    // norm_sq = sum_i (||g_i||_2)^2, accumulated in fp32 on-device, one sync.
204	    auto stacked = torch::stack(norms).to(torch::kFloat32);
205	    float total_norm =
206	        std::sqrt(stacked.dot(stacked).item<float>());
207	
208	    if (total_norm > grad_clip_norm) {
209	        float clip_coef = grad_clip_norm / (total_norm + 1e-6f);
210	        // Fused multi-tensor in-place scale of the present grads.
211	        torch::_foreach_mul_(present, clip_coef);
212	    }
213	}

215	// ── Device-side SAM grad-norm: single CPU sync instead of N ──────────
216	inline float compute_sam_grad_norm_device_side(
217	    std::vector<torch::Tensor>& grads,
218	    size_t n_grads
219	) {
220	    torch::Device dev(torch::kCPU);
221	    for (size_t i = 0; i < n_grads; i++) {
222	        if (grads[i].defined() && grads[i].numel() > 0) {
223	            dev = grads[i].device();
224	            break;
225	        }
226	    }
227	    auto norm_sq = torch::zeros(
228	        {1}, torch::TensorOptions().device(dev).dtype(torch::kFloat32));
229	    for (size_t i = 0; i < n_grads; i++) {
230	        if (grads[i].defined() && grads[i].numel() > 0) {
231	            auto g_flat = grads[i].to(torch::kFloat32).reshape(-1);
232	            norm_sq.add_(g_flat.dot(g_flat));
233	        }
234	    }
235	    return std::sqrt(norm_sq.item<float>()) + 1e-12f;
236	}

181	// csrc/common/ops.cpp::grokadamw_fused_step. Loops over per-param

185	void grokadamw_fused_step(
186	 std::vector<torch::Tensor>& params,
187	 std::vector<torch::Tensor>& grads,
188	 std::vector<torch::Tensor>& exp_avgs,
189	 std::vector<torch::Tensor>& exp_avg_sqs,
190	 std::vector<torch::Tensor>& emas,
191	 std::vector<int64_t>& steps,
192	 float alpha, float lamb_grok,
193	 float beta1, float beta2, float lr, float wd,
194	 float eps, float grad_clip_norm
195	) {
196	 const size_t n_params = params.size();
197	 check_params_grads(params, grads, "grokadamw_fused_step");
198	 clip_grad_norms_device_side(grads, n_params, grad_clip_norm);
199	 if (n_params == 0) return;
200	
201	 // NOTE: the Python optimizer owns the step counter (state["step"] += 1
202	 // before this call), matching fused_adamw_simple_step and
203	 // grokfast_fused_ema_adam_step. Do NOT increment here — `steps` is a
204	 // pybind-copied vector so an increment would not persist back to Python
205	 // anyway, and incrementing made bias correction permanently off-by-one
206	 // (bc computed with step+1).
207	
208	 // Common case: every param has a grad. Then the per-tensor lists are just
209	 // the inputs verbatim, so we skip rebuilding the 5 parallel filtered tensor
210	 // vectors (vp/vg/vea/veas/vema) and pass the originals straight through. The
211	 // bias-correction scalars are intrinsically per-param and still computed.
212	 bool all_present = true;
213	 for (size_t i = 0; i < n_params; i++) {
214	 if (!grads[i].defined() || grads[i].numel() == 0) { all_present = false; break; }
215	 }
216	
217	 if (all_present) {
218	 std::vector<float> bc1_vec, bc2_vec;
219	 bc1_vec.reserve(n_params); bc2_vec.reserve(n_params);
220	 for (size_t i = 0; i < n_params; i++) {
221	 bc1_vec.push_back(1.0f - std::pow(beta1, static_cast<float>(steps[i])));
222	 bc2_vec.push_back(1.0f - std::pow(beta2, static_cast<float>(steps[i])));
223	 }
224	 DISPATCH_GROKADAMW(launch_multi_tensor_grokadamw,
225	 params, exp_avgs, exp_avg_sqs, emas, grads, bc1_vec, bc2_vec,
226	 alpha, lamb_grok, beta1, beta2, lr, wd, eps);
227	 }
228	
229	 // Sparse-grad fallback: build the filtered parallel vectors.
230	 std::vector<torch::Tensor> vp, vg, vea, veas, vema;
231	 std::vector<float> bc1_vec, bc2_vec;
232	 for (size_t i = 0; i < n_params; i++) {
233	 if (!grads[i].defined() || grads[i].numel() == 0) continue;
234	 float bc1 = 1.0f - std::pow(beta1, static_cast<float>(steps[i]));
235	 float bc2 = 1.0f - std::pow(beta2, static_cast<float>(steps[i]));
236	 vp.push_back(params[i]); vg.push_back(grads[i]);
237	 vea.push_back(exp_avgs[i]); veas.push_back(exp_avg_sqs[i]);
238	 vema.push_back(emas[i]);
239	 bc1_vec.push_back(bc1); bc2_vec.push_back(bc2);
240	 }
241	 if (vp.empty()) return;
242	
243	 DISPATCH_GROKADAMW(launch_multi_tensor_grokadamw,
244	 vp, vea, veas, vema, vg, bc1_vec, bc2_vec,
245	 alpha, lamb_grok, beta1, beta2, lr, wd, eps);
246	}

913	// High-level vector-signature entry point — pre-refactor
914	// csrc/common/ops.cpp::muon_fused_step. The math is unchanged.
915	// Replaces N CPU syncs with one (torch::stack of bufs[i].norm()).
916	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------
917	
918	void muon_fused_step(
919	 std::vector<torch::Tensor>& params,
920	 std::vector<torch::Tensor>& grads,
921	 std::vector<torch::Tensor>& bufs,
922	 float momentum, float lr, float wd, int ns_steps
923	) {
924	 check_params_grads(params, grads, "muon_fused_step");
925	 constexpr float NS_A = 3.4445f;
926	 constexpr float NS_B = -4.7750f;
927	 constexpr float NS_C = 2.0315f;
928	
929	 std::vector<torch::Tensor> norm_tensors;
930	 std::vector<size_t> valid_indices;
931	 norm_tensors.reserve(params.size());
932	 valid_indices.reserve(params.size());
933	 for (size_t i = 0; i < params.size(); i++) {
934	 if (!grads[i].defined() || grads[i].numel() == 0) continue;
935	 bufs[i].mul_(momentum).add_(grads[i]);
936	 norm_tensors.push_back(bufs[i].norm());
937	 valid_indices.push_back(i);
938	 }
939	 if (norm_tensors.empty()) return;
940	
941	 auto norms_stacked = torch::stack(norm_tensors).cpu();
942	 auto* norms_ptr = norms_stacked.data_ptr<float>();
943	
944	 for (size_t vi = 0; vi < valid_indices.size(); vi++) {
945	 size_t i = valid_indices[vi];
946	 auto& p = params[i];
947	 auto& buf = bufs[i];
948	
949	 float buf_norm = norms_ptr[vi] + 1e-7f;
950	 float inv_norm = 1.0f / buf_norm;
951	 auto X = buf * inv_norm;
952	
953	 // Muon's Newton-Schulz orthogonalization (X.t(), mm) and the
954	 // 0.2*sqrt(max(rows,cols)) RMS scale are defined only for a 2D
955	 // matrix param. A 1D bias or a 3D/4D conv weight would silently read
956	 // p.size(1) as a wrong dimension (or be undefined for dim<2) and
957	 // corrupt the update. The Python Muon optimizer routes non-2D params
958	 // to the AdamW path (fused_adamw_simple_step); enforce that contract
959	 // loudly here so a misrouted param fails instead of corrupting.
960	 TORCH_CHECK(p.dim() == 2, "muon_fused_step: param ", i,
961	 " has ndim=", p.dim(),
962	 " but the Newton-Schulz orthogonalization requires a 2D "
963	 "matrix. Route 1D/>=3D params to the AdamW path "
964	 "(fused_adamw_simple_step) in the Python wrapper.");
965	 int64_t rows = p.size(0);
966	 int64_t cols = p.size(1);
967	 float max_dim = static_cast<float>(std::max(rows, cols));
968	 float scale_factor = 0.2f * std::sqrt(max_dim);
969	 float neg_lr_scale = -lr * scale_factor;
970	 float decay_factor = 1.0f - lr * wd;
971	
972	 // Double-buffer the NS combine output: allocate one scratch of X's shape
973	 // up front and ping-pong into it across iterations, instead of a fresh
974	 // torch::empty_like(X) every intermediate step. The combine launcher reads
975	 // X and writes a distinct buffer, so two buffers suffice; we swap handles
976	 // (no copies). Math is unchanged.
977	 torch::Tensor scratch; // lazily allocated on first combine step
978	 for (int step = 0; step < ns_steps; step++) {
979	 auto A = torch::mm(X, X.t());
980	 auto AX = torch::mm(A, X);
981	 auto AAX = torch::mm(A, AX);
982	 if (step < ns_steps - 1) {
983	 if (!scratch.defined()) scratch = torch::empty_like(X);
984	 SG_DISPATCH_CALL(launch_muon_ns_combine,
985	 scratch, X, AX, AAX, NS_A, NS_B, NS_C);
986	 // Ping-pong: the just-read X becomes the next iteration's scratch,
987	 // the freshly-written buffer becomes X.
988	 std::swap(X, scratch);
989	 } else {
990	 SG_DISPATCH_CALL(launch_muon_ns_combine_update_fused,
991	 p, X, AX, AAX, NS_A, NS_B, NS_C,
992	 neg_lr_scale, decay_factor);
993	 }
994	 }
995	 if (ns_steps == 0) {
996	 auto X_typed = X.to(p.dtype());
997	 SG_DISPATCH_CALL(launch_muon_update,
998	 p, X_typed, neg_lr_scale, decay_factor);
999	 }
